title: Restart is not a diagnosis
summary: Use a deterministic Linux shell to read a failed unit, fix permissions, clear a port conflict, and verify recovery.

scenario.briefing: The orders API stopped after a configuration deploy. The unit is failed, the database service is stopped, and an old process still holds port 8080. Work in the simulated shell: read the evidence, fix only what is broken, and bring the stack up in the right order.

objectives.description: Find the permission failure in the service log.
Give the config file the smallest readable mode.
Clear the stale process holding the port.
Restart the API and confirm it is running.
Apply the diagnosis discipline to a new incident.

hints: Read the file mode before changing it.
Check ps for the process holding port 8080.
Fix the mode, kill the stale process, start inventory-db, then restart orders-api.

misconceptions.feedback: A restart repeats the same failure and can push the original error out of view. Read the journal first.

misconceptions.description: Making the config world-readable and world-writable.
misconceptions.feedback: The service only needs to read its config. Use a mode such as 640 and keep ownership with the service account.

misconceptions.description: Starting the API before its database dependency.
misconceptions.feedback: Start dependencies first. The API cannot become ready while the database is down.

misconceptions.description: Believing a restart is itself a diagnostic step.
misconceptions.feedback: A restart changes state and can hide the failure. Read the journal, then fix the cause and verify recovery.

sections.title: Read the failure before changing state
sections.body: systemctl status shows the unit state; journalctl -u shows what the process actually reported. A restart destroys the failing state and may hide the cause. Read first, then change one thing.

sections.title: Permissions belong to the service identity
sections.body: Compare the file owner and mode with the user the unit runs as. Grant read access, not world write. A broad mode such as 777 makes the symptom disappear while widening access for every local account.

sections.title: Dependencies have an order
sections.body: The API needs its database. A port conflict is a separate failure: find the stale process with ps, terminate it, then start the dependency and restart the service. Verify with status and a health request.

steps.title: Recover the orders API
steps.prompt: Use the simulated shell. The unit is failed, a stale process holds port 8080, and the database service is stopped. Read the evidence, fix the config mode, clear the conflict, start the dependency, and restart the API.
hints: Run journalctl -u orders-api and read the last lines.
The config file is /srv/campus/app/config.json; inspect it with ls -l.
Run ps to find the process holding port 8080, then kill it by pid.
Use chmod 640 config.json, systemctl start inventory-db, then systemctl restart orders-api.

files.content:
[Unit]
Description=Orders API
After=network.target inventory-db.service

[Service]
User=campus
WorkingDirectory=/srv/campus/app
ExecStart=/usr/bin/node server.js
Restart=on-failure

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target

objectives.description: Read the permission failure in the orders-api journal.
Terminate the stale process holding port 8080.
Restart orders-api and leave it running.

steps.explanation: The journal showed a permission failure, the config mode was too narrow, a stale process held the port, and the database was down. Each fix addressed one cause, and the restart was verified by state.

steps.title: Diagnosis that transfers
hints: Read the failure before changing state.
A service is ready only when its dependencies are ready.
A port conflict is separate from a permission error.
Select evidence-first diagnosis, least privilege, dependency order, and verification; reject restart-first.

statements.label: The journal and unit definition are evidence about why the service failed.
Grant the service only the file access it needs.
Start and verify dependencies before the service that needs them.
A restart is complete only after the unit is running and a health check passes.
Restarting repeatedly is a reliable way to find the root cause.

steps.explanation: Diagnosis reads evidence, changes one cause at a time with least privilege, respects dependency order, and verifies recovery.
